categories.name: Thinking
criteria: Simple development using reasons or details

categories.name: Communication & Structure
criteria: Effective introduction (tells what the writing is about)
One main idea in the body paragraph
At least one supporting detail sentence
Clear conclusion (wraps up the main idea)

categories.name: Application
criteria: Basic sentence control (avoid fragments/run-ons when possible)
Punctuation (periods, question marks, commas in simple lists)

scoreMeaning.description: Clear structure and strong overall writing, as appropriate for the student's grade
Structure present but needs improvement, as appropriate for the student's grade
Structure incomplete or unclear; revision required, based on grade-level expectations
Major gaps in grade-level writing fundamentals

gradingPrinciples: Evaluate writing based on Grade 3 expectations only.
Do not apply Grade 4+ standards (length, sophistication, or advanced reasoning).
Prioritize structure and clarity over complexity.
Apply spelling and language conventions according to the specified language variant.

softGuidelines: Use familiar, concrete topics (school, home, friends, hobbies, nature).
Prompts must be answerable without research.
Keep prompts short and very clear.
Encourage 1–2 simple reasons or a few clear details (no counterarguments).
